dsh-profile-stats
A personal usage profile page in the DSH sidebar.
How many tokens you have burned, when, on which model, and through which billing route —
all folded from this machine's own session logs.
English · 简体中文
## Install
In DSH open **Plugins → Add plugin** and paste the package name:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What you get
| | Section | What it shows |
| 📊 | **Five headline numbers** | Tokens in the selected range (with daily bars for 7 / 30 days or a
7-day average trend for longer ranges, and the change against the previous period), today's tokens,

longest task, the active-day streak with your best, today's cache hit rate |
| 🗓️ | **Token activit

y** | A 12-month day grid, switchable between daily, weekly and running-total views |
| 🧩 | **Model
distribution** | Stacked columns by model family (version + tier, so `v4-flash` and `v4.1-flash` sta
y apart) over the selected range, by day, week or month, as token amounts or as each bucket's share

|
| 🎯 | **Cache Lens** | Total tokens plus the cache hit rate, and the cache-hit / uncached-input /
output split (plus cache write when a provider reports it) as a segmented bar, with a zoom into the

uncached part and the daily cache hit rate underneath |
| 💳 | **Provider split** | Tokens and cache
hit rate per billing route in the selected range, or today only; give a route a display name that st

ays on your machine |
| 📁 | **Projects** | Tokens per working directory in the selected range, with
the part used by subagent sessions |
A range switch in the header — 7 / 30 / 90 days, this month, all time or custom dates — drives the f
irst number, the model distribution, Cache Lens, the projects and the provider split; the selected r
ange can be exported as CSV (one row per day) or JSON.
## Privacy

> [!NOTE]
> Everything is read from your own session logs through `ctx.sessionQuery`; nothing is re-

derived
> from guesses. The only outbound request is a six-hourly read of this package's own version

from
> the npm registry, used by the in-panel update button. No telemetry, no credentials, nothing

> uploaded.
